raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
### What does this PR do?

Fixes #8406.

`compute_policy_loss_geo_mean` folded IcePop-rejected tokens (IS weight 0) into the geometric mean through `log(1e-10)` and left them in the policy ratio: a rejected token kept its gradient and the rest of its sequence was down-scaled (x0.24 at L=16, x0.70 at L=64 in the issue's CPU repro).

The fix applies one rule, mirroring the token-level losses: a rejected token contributes exactly 0 to every geo_mean sum while denominators stay the original token count, so kept tokens keep the gradient they had without the rejection. A fully rejected sequence gets zero weight instead of a loss built from the sequence advantage alone. Diagnostics (`ppo_kl`, clip fractions) still use the original `response_mask` and are unchanged.

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Search for similar PRs. Open geo_mean work found: #7916 (minibatch normalization for geo_mean), #5614 (agg_loss DP consistency), #7913 (issue: minibatch-split sensitivity). None of them changes the `seq_is_weights` computation, which the issue itself confirms, so this is not a duplicate. Search: https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+geo_mean
- [x] Format the PR title as `[{modules}] {type}: {description}`

### Test

CPU-only host; GPU suites and full `make test` were not run locally (CI covers them).

Repro from the issue (`B=2, L=16`, token 5 of sequence 1 rejected by IcePop):
- Before: `[vanilla] grad -0.00000, ratio 1.000` / `[geo_mean] grad -0.00741, ratio 0.237`
- After: `[vanilla] grad -0.00000, ratio 1.000` / `[geo_mean] grad -0.00000, ratio 1.000`

New regression test `test_geo_mean_drops_icepop_rejected_tokens` in `tests/trainer/ppo/test_core_algos_on_cpu.py` (CPU CI file, matching the `*_on_cpu.py` pattern): fails on pristine main, passes with the fix. It also covers the fully rejected sequence (zero loss contribution, zero gradient).

```
PYTHONPATH=. .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/trainer/ppo/test_core_algos_on_cpu.py -q
# 24 passed
```

`ruff check` and `ruff format --check` are clean on both touched files (run scoped to these files, not full `pre-commit run --all-files`).

### API and Usage Example

No API change. `compute_policy_loss_geo_mean` keeps its signature; behaviour only changes when `rollout_is_weights` contains zeros (IcePop rejections). With all-positive weights the output is bit-identical to before.

### Design & Code Changes

- `verl/trainer/ppo/core_algos.py` (`compute_policy_loss_geo_mean`): build `loss_mask = response_mask * (rollout_is_weights > 0)` and use it in the ratio and IS-aggregation numerators; denominators stay `response_mask_sum`; zero `pg_losses` where a sequence has no kept tokens.
- `tests/trainer/ppo/test_core_algos_on_cpu.py`: regression test above.

### Checklist Before Submitting

- [x] Read the [Contribute Guide](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) (plus `AGENTS.md`: duplicate checks done above, AI assistance disclosed below).
- [ ] Apply [pre-commit checks](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#code-linting-and-formatting): `ruff` was run scoped to the two touched files (clean); full `pre-commit run --all-files` was not run locally.
- [ ] Add / Update [the documentation](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/tree/main/docs): not applicable, the `docs/algo/rollout_corr.md` statement (IcePop only changes IS coefficients, not `response_mask`) is still true and unchanged by this fix.
- [x] Add unit test(s) to [the CI workflow](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/tree/main/.github/workflows) to cover the code: test added to `tests/trainer/ppo/test_core_algos_on_cpu.py`, which the CPU workflow picks up via its `*_on_cpu.py` pattern; no workflow change needed.
- [ ] Once your PR is ready for CI, send a message in the `ci-request` channel: for the account owner to do (Slack access is human-only).

### AI assistance disclosure (per AGENTS.md)

AI assistance was used for this PR (tool: Muse, Meta's personal AI agent): investigating the issue, writing the fix and the regression test, and running the local verification above. The human submitter still needs to review every changed line and run the relevant tests before this is merged.

files.patch:
@@ -24,12 +24,16 @@
     compute_gae_advantage_return,
     compute_grpo_outcome_advantage,
     compute_grpo_vectorized_outcome_advantage,
+    compute_policy_loss_geo_mean,
+    compute_policy_loss_vanilla,
     compute_rloo_outcome_advantage,
     compute_rloo_vectorized_outcome_advantage,
     get_adv_estimator_fn,
     kl_penalty,
     register_adv_est,
 )
+from verl.trainer.ppo.rollout_corr_helper import compute_rollout_correction_and_rejection_mask
+from verl.workers.config.actor import ActorConfig, PolicyLossConfig
 
 
 def mock_test_fn():
@@ -381,5 +385,83 @@ def test_kl_penalty_k3_plus_uses_k2_gradient():
     assert torch.allclose(grad_plus, grad_k2)
 
 
+def test_geo_mean_drops_icepop_rejected_tokens():
+    """geo_mean must drop IcePop-rejected tokens entirely (see #8406).
+
+    A token whose IcePop weight is 0 keeps no gradient, and the kept tokens
+    in its sequence keep the gradient they had without the rejection (the
+    same behaviour as the token-level losses). A fully rejected sequence
+    contributes zero loss and zero gradient.
+    """
+
+    def actor_config(loss_mode):
+        return ActorConfig(
+            strategy="fsdp",
+            rollout_n=1,
+            ppo_micro_batch_size_per_gpu=1,
+            clip_ratio=0.2,
+            clip_ratio_low=0.2,
+            clip_ratio_high=0.2,
+            loss_agg_mode="token-mean",
+            policy_loss=PolicyLossConfig(loss_mode=loss_mode),
+        )
+
+    batch_size, seq_len, bad = 2, 16, 5
+    old_log_prob = torch.full((batch_size, seq_len), -1.0)
+    rollout_log_prob = old_log_prob.clone()
+    rollout_log_prob[1, bad] = -4.0  # old/rollout ratio e^3 ~ 20, outside IcePop's [0.5, 5.0]
+    response_mask = torch.ones(batch_size, seq_len)
+    advantages = torch.ones(batch_size, seq_len)
+
+    weights_proto, _, _ = compute_rollout_correction_and_rejection_mask(
+        old_log_prob=old_log_prob,
+        rollout_log_prob=rollout_log_prob,
+        response_mask=response_mask,
+        rollout_is="token",
+        rollout_is_threshold="0.5_5.0",
+    )
+    weights = weights_proto.batch["rollout_is_weights"]
+    assert weights[1, bad].item() == 0.0, "bad token must be rejected by IcePop"
+    assert weights[0].min().item() > 0.0, "clean sequence must keep all weights"
+
+    grads = {}
+    for loss_mode, fn in [("vanilla", compute_policy_loss_vanilla), ("geo_mean", compute_policy_loss_geo_mean)]:
+        log_prob = old_log_prob.clone().requires_grad_(True)  # on-policy
+        loss, _ = fn(
+            old_log_prob=old_log_prob,
+            log_prob=log_prob,
+            advantages=advantages,
+            response_mask=response_mask,
+            loss_agg_mode="token-mean",
+            config=actor_config(loss_mode),
+            rollout_is_weights=weights,
+        )
+        loss.backward()
+        grads[loss_mode] = log_prob.grad
+
+    for loss_mode in ("vanilla", "geo_mean"):
+        g = grads[loss_mode]
+        assert g[1, bad].item() == pytest.approx(0.0, abs=1e-6), f"{loss_mode}: rejected token must have no grad"
+        kept_ratio = g[1, 0].item() / g[0, 0].item()
+        assert kept_ratio == pytest.approx(1.0, abs=1e-3), f"{loss_mode}: kept-token grad ratio {kept_ratio}"
+
+    # Fully rejected sequence: zero loss contribution, zero gradient.
+    full_reject_weights = torch.ones(batch_size, seq_len)
+    full_reject_weights[1, :] = 0.0
+    log_prob = old_log_prob.clone().requires_grad_(True)
+    loss, _ = compute_policy_loss_geo_mean(
+        old_log_prob=old_log_prob,
+        log_prob=log_prob,
+        advantages=advantages,
+        response_mask=response_mask,
+        loss_agg_mode="token-mean",
+        config=actor_config("geo_mean"),
+        rollout_is_weights=full_reject_weights,
+    )
+    loss.backward()
+    assert loss.item() == pytest.approx(-0.5, abs=1e-6), "fully rejected sequence must contribute 0 to the batch mean"
+    assert float(log_prob.grad[1].abs().max()) == pytest.approx(0.0, abs=1e-6)
+
+
 if __name__ == "__main__":
     unittest.main()

@@ -1981,7 +1981,18 @@ def compute_policy_loss_geo_mean(
 
     # Geometric-Mean Policy Optimization
     response_mask_sum = response_mask.sum(dim=-1)
-    ratio = torch.exp((negative_approx_kl_min * response_mask).sum(dim=-1) / (response_mask_sum + 1e-8))
+    # When rollout correction weights are provided, tokens rejected by IcePop
+    # (weight 0) must drop out of the loss entirely: they keep no gradient and
+    # must not change the weight of the other tokens in their sequence.
+    # Folding them in with the plain response_mask would add log(1e-10) to the
+    # geometric mean and leave the rejected token in the policy ratio
+    # (see #8406). The rule mirrors the token-level losses: a rejected token
+    # contributes exactly 0 to every sum while denominators stay unchanged, so
+    # kept tokens keep the gradient they had without the rejection.
+    loss_mask = response_mask
+    if rollout_is_weights is not None:
+        loss_mask = response_mask * (rollout_is_weights > 0).to(response_mask.dtype)
+    ratio = torch.exp((negative_approx_kl_min * loss_mask).sum(dim=-1) / (response_mask_sum + 1e-8))
     # we only support sequence level advantage for now,
     # otherwise, below would be not consistent with the paper
     advantage = (advantages * response_mask).sum(dim=-1) / (response_mask_sum + 1e-8)
@@ -1992,10 +2003,15 @@ def compute_policy_loss_geo_mean(
     if rollout_is_weights is not None:
         # Aggregate token-level weights to sequence level using geometric mean for consistency
         # Note: rollout_is_weights is always 2D regardless of aggregation mode
+        # Rejected tokens contribute 0 to the log-sum (loss_mask), while the
+        # denominator stays the original token count, as above.
         seq_is_weights = torch.exp(
-            (torch.log(rollout_is_weights + 1e-10) * response_mask).sum(dim=-1) / (response_mask_sum + 1e-8)
+            (torch.log(rollout_is_weights + 1e-10) * loss_mask).sum(dim=-1) / (response_mask_sum + 1e-8)
         )
         pg_losses = pg_losses * seq_is_weights
+        # A fully rejected sequence has no kept tokens, so it gets zero weight
+        # rather than a loss built from the sequence advantage alone.
+        pg_losses = pg_losses * (loss_mask.sum(dim=-1) > 0).to(pg_losses.dtype)
 
     pg_loss = torch.mean(pg_losses)
